rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; i1040sca p. 11, Other Itemized Deductions: "Gambling losses ... but only to the extent of gambling winnings reported on Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 8b". With no winnings line 16 is zero whatever the losses, so sa.gambling_losses is not needed; the project asks it only when s1.gambling_winnings is positive, the reading chosen in amb.2025.gambling_losses ("with no winnings it is zero and the losses are not asked"). The candidate's unguarded smaller_of needs the losses on every return; complete-record arithmetic agrees, availability does not. Triage executable-triage-v1 (triage/sa.json): 879 of 2,120 agree; 1,116 candidate-unknown records have no winnings and no losses answer (classm.f2441.1.deepseek to .6.deepseek recorded, project $0.00); 91 project-refuses and 34 project-unknown come from the project also declaring sa.charity_limited and sa.excluded_income on line 16 (classm.f8606.1, classm.refund.1: charity_limited; classm.s179.3: excluded_income; partials withholding those screens from classm.f8889.2.deepseek, classm.f5695.3), screens line 17 declares too, so Schedule A and line 12e are refused on the same returns either way (scope). Project stands.

Ruling: equivalent; project retained. With no gambling winnings line 8b is zero, so the smaller of the losses and line 8b is zero, which the project writes as an explicit zero; with winnings both give the losses up to line 8b (i1040sca p. 11, Other Itemized Deductions, "Gambling losses ... but only to the extent of gambling winnings reported on Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 8b"; decision D14). The project's guard asks the losses only of a filer with winnings.

Ruling: scope; i1040sca p. 7, State and Local Tax Deduction Worksheet: "1. ... Enter $40,000", "5. Enter $500,000 ($250,000 if married filing separately)", "6. ... Skip lines 7 and 8 and enter the amount from line 1 on line 9", line 9 the larger of line 8 or $10,000. The candidate writes larger_of(line 8, $10,000) as $10,000 plus the excess of a signed line 8 over $10,000, which is the same amount, and halves it for MFS as the project does; the formulas agree on every return. The differences are refusals the candidate places on lines 5d and 5e (sa.unsupported, sa.excluded_income) where the project places them on lines 16 and 17 and sa.deduction. Triage executable-triage-v1 (triage/sa.json): 2,006 of 2,120 agree, no value differences; 52 candidate-refuses on sa.excluded_income (classm.retirement.3, classm.s179.3, stage12.excluded_income_no_claim) are returns on which the project refuses sa.line17 and Form 1040 line 12e through the same cited gate (checked on stage12.excluded_income_no_claim); 53 candidate-unknown are partial records withholding sa.unsupported, which every interview asks for line 17 (bases classm.f2441.1.deepseek, classm.f8889.2.deepseek, classm.f4952.2); 9 project-refuses are foreign cited gates reached through f1040.line11b (f8889 unsupported, retirement special, sales digital, sb.form8938) on records that omit or withhold sa.excluded_income, where the candidate stops first on its own gate. Project stands.

Ruling: equivalent representation; project retained. The second transcription applies the State and Local Tax Deduction Worksheet only when modified AGI exceeds $500,000 or income was excluded, and otherwise takes the $40,000 base directly; the project computes the worksheet unconditionally, where the reduction is zero at or below the threshold and the excluded-income case is refused (`sa.excluded_income`). Same value within scope (i1040sca p. 7).

Ruling: model error; f1040s1a, line 36a: "If you have a valid social security number (see instructions) and were born before January 2, 1961, enter the amount from line 35", with the spouse on line 36b ("If you are married filing jointly, your spouse has a valid social security number ... and your spouse was born before January 2, 1961"); i1040gi p. 33, line 12d, likewise separates the boxes for you and for your spouse. sa.age65 is the question "Were you born before January 2, 1961?" for you alone (Schedule 1-A line 36a reads it); the candidate also counts the spouse (on a joint return, or MFS with spouse boxes). Triage executable-triage-v1 (triage/sa.json): 2,070 of 2,120 agree; all 50 differences are value, project False against candidate True, on joint returns where only the spouse was born before January 2, 1961 (classm.asset.1: taxpayer age65 false, spouse true; classm.otjob.1, classm.s1a.1, classm.sc.1, classm.scveh.4, classm.se.1), where the candidate would put the taxpayer's senior deduction on line 36a. The reviewer did not receive f1040s1a, but the interface label "Were you born before January 2, 1961?" and i1040gi p. 33 (given), which separates the boxes for you and for your spouse, decide the reading. Project stands.

Ruling: equivalent; project retained. Both test whether your own person entry answers yes to born before January 2, 1961: the project as a count above zero, the second as a count of at least one; a count is a whole number, so the tests agree (i1040gi p. 33, Line 12d, "If you or your spouse (if you are married and filing a joint return) were born before January 2, 1961").

Checked by evaluation: joint return, wages $60,000 and $50,000, spouse born in 1960, no work SSN, died in 2025 before 65: Form 1040 line 12e $33,100 and line 15 $76,900, unrefused; the text gives $31,500 and $78,500.
